lesson: An unreadable config.yaml (missing, permission error) returns [] and is treated as 'no presets configured'. The build then proceeds with only base and exits 0, so 'could not read config' reads as 'nothing configured'. Distinguish the missing/unreadable case: warn on stderr and exit non-zero (or at least exit 1).

The parser only understands the inline `[..]` and block-list forms. Any other shape (e.g. `presets: python` scalar, `presets: []` mixed with comments, CRLF line endings, `presets:  # comment` followed by a list, or a `presets:` key nested under another section) silently yields [] and exit 0 instead of flagging a malformed value. Fail closed: if a `presets:` key is present but no form matched, warn and exit 1.

`Extends:` is matched only when the file's first non-blank line is exactly that; the README and header comment say 'start the file with Extends', but a `Extends: x` with trailing text, in different case, or after a `# Preset:` title line is silently ignored and the local file replaces the built-in with no warning. Also `Extends: <other>` where <other> is neither local nor built-in yields (parent, None), reported unknown, but a local preset extending a name that itself extends is silently single-level. Additionally the extends() open() has no error handling (non-UTF-8 file raises a traceback, exit 1 with no 'unknown preset' message).

Tests cover only the inline `[..]` config form. The block-list parser branch, `Extends: other-name` (non-self), local-extends-local, dedupe, missing config, and the Extends-not-first-line case have no tests, so the variants of this resolver are unproven. Also AC-5 only checks the exit code with the `../x` name; it does not verify that no file outside presets/ is read.

AC-6 asserts $TMP/n/.specclaw/presets/README.md exists but the diff never creates $TMP/n in the added lines; it depends on an earlier fixture elsewhere in the file. If that fixture does not run specclaw-init, the check is vacuous or fails for the wrong reason, and it does not verify init content matches the template.

The Extends fix is an instance fix. It added case-insensitivity and heading-skipping, but the named 'trailing text' variant still matches nothing. The regex needs the whole line to be `extends: <one-token>`, so any other line returns None. A local preset then silently replaces the built-in, with no warning and exit 0. A malformed Extends declaration (the line starts with `extends` but does not parse) should be warned and exit 1 instead of being treated as 'no Extends'. Also decide and document what happens when prose or an HTML comment precedes the Extends line.

The block-list branch still fails open for malformed shapes. The loop breaks on the first line that does not start with `- `, so it cannot tell a new top-level key from garbage inside the list. Garbage includes an indented scalar, a bare `-`, `-python` and `- ` with a tab. Everything after that line is silently dropped, and the key then yields a short or empty list with exit 0. Break only on a column-0 non-dash line (a new key). Warn on any other unparsable line under `presets:`.

The variant table still lacks cases the previous round named. There is no dedupe row (`[python, python]` or `[base]`) and no row for Extends placed after non-heading text or carrying trailing text. There is no row for a malformed block list (indented scalar, bare `-`), which would have exposed the B6 gap. The symlink case covers only a direct preset file, not an Extends parent that is a symlink. AC-5 (`../x`) still asserts only the exit code, not that nothing outside presets/ is read.

The AC-6 'fix' is only a comment. It claims the $TMP/n tree comes from an AC-10 case 'above', and that cannot be checked from the diff. The test still depends on a fixture elsewhere in the file. It still asserts only that the README exists, not that its content matches the init template. Drive specclaw-init into a fresh dir within this test and compare the file to the template (`cmp`).

The Extends check is now too broad. It scans every non-heading line in the file, with no fence or position awareness. Any line that starts with the word `extends` is treated as a malformed or misplaced Extends declaration, including ordinary prose. That prose line triggers the warning and an exit-1 failure for a valid preset that never declared Extends. Only a line that looks like a declaration (`extends` followed by optional spaces and a colon) should be an error. A prose line that merely begins with the word should be ignored, and the match should skip fenced code blocks. Add a regression row for this.

The new symlinked-Extends-parent check only asserts `! specclaw-presets | grep -q outside.md`, with no exit-code assertion. The sibling direct-symlink check has both. Output lines are label-style (`v:a`, `specclaw:base`), so the symlink named b.md would print as `v:b` or a b.md path and never contain `outside.md`. The grep is then vacuously true even if the symlink guard were removed for Extends parents. Assert exit 1 and the exact stdout (`specclaw:base v:a `). Better still, assert that the parent's content ('secret') is absent from the build output.

A file that does not open with `---` now returns None silently. This includes the old `Extends: <name>` first-line form, any case or spelling variant, and the common mistake of using `extends:` without frontmatter. The local file then silently replaces the built-in, which is the wrong-intent fallback the earlier rounds treated as an error. The prose-collision fix should have kept a narrow check: warn and exit 1 only when a non-heading line outside any fence matches `^extends\s*:`, as the previous round proposed. Prose such as 'Extends the base rules.' would still pass.

The fix only handles part of the fenced-code case. `stray()` treats only a line starting with three backticks as a fence. Three variants are wrong: (1) a `~~~` fence is not recognised, so a documented `extends: node` inside it is reported as an error, which is a false positive that blocks the whole build. (2) Every line is `.strip()`ped before the check, so an indented code block or an indented list continuation line `    extends: node` is also flagged. (3) An unclosed ``` fence hides every later line, so a real stray `extends:` after it is silently ignored. That is the fail-open case this fix was meant to close. Track the fence character and length, and close only on a matching fence. Check the indentation-sensitive form on the raw line instead of the stripped one. Warn when a fence is still open at end of file.

The variant table for the stray-`extends:` check covers only the backtick fence. It has no rows for a `~~~` fence, an indented `extends:` line, an unclosed fence followed by `extends:`, `Extends : node` with a space before the colon, or a heading containing the word. Without these rows the instance fix above passes while the variants misbehave. Add them to the table.

The variants the previous round named are still missing from the table. Only one row asserts that the warning is emitted (`# Ours\nExtends: node`). The other stray rows (not-on-line-1, after-fm, the fenced row) assert only `exit 0` plus the label list, and those are identical whether `stray()` warns or not. Add warning-assertion rows for: a `~~~` fence, an unclosed fence followed by `extends:`, `Extends : node` with a space before the colon, and a heading containing the word. Add negative rows asserting no warning for an indented `    extends: node` and for valid frontmatter. Also make the new check create its own `$TMP/v` fixture instead of reusing the directory left by the previous `cfgcase`. The explicit `printf` writes are fine, but the dir and `presets/` must exist from earlier cases.

Extends is followed only one level, and the parent's own frontmatter is never read or checked. When a local preset extends another local preset that has its own frontmatter, that parent's `extends:` is silently dropped and the run exits 0. A malformed parent frontmatter (other key, unclosed) is not reported either. The README shows both `extends: dotnet` inside dotnet.md and adding a new `acme-dotnet`, so chaining them is the obvious use, and the README never says 'one level'. Fix: run `extends()` on a local parent too. Either follow it, with a cycle guard, or warn fatally that a nested extends is ignored. Add rows for a two-level chain, a malformed parent frontmatter and a self or mutual cycle.

`lookup` returns None for 'no such file' and also for 'a file is there but cannot be used': a dangling symlink, a directory named `<name>.md`, or a non-regular file. `resolve` reads None as 'no local preset' and silently substitutes the built-in. Fix: if `os.path.lexists(p)` is true but the path is not a usable regular file, warn fatally and do not fall back. Add rows for a dangling symlink and for a directory.

The BOM handling (`utf-8-sig`) was applied to preset files but not to config.yaml, which is read as plain `utf-8`. A BOM-prefixed first line `\ufeffpresets: [..]` fails `^presets:`. `configured()` then returns [] exactly as if no presets were configured, and exits 0. Fix: open config.yaml with `utf-8-sig`. Add a 'BOM before presets:' row next to the existing CRLF rows.

The nested-extends check treats any parent with frontmatter as nesting. That includes a local parent that only extends its own built-in (`dotnet.md` with `extends: dotnet`), which is the documented way to keep a built-in. A valid two-file setup therefore fails the build, and when only the child is listed the built-in parent is silently dropped from the output. Exempt `extends(local_parent) == parent` and emit the built-in before the local parent, or warn non-fatally when that parent is already resolved earlier in `out`. Add table rows for both orders.

Scalar parsing exists twice and the copies disagree. `strip()` (config values) strips any mix of quote characters, while `extends()` uses a regex with a back-reference that requires matched quotes. The same malformed value is accepted in config.yaml and rejected in frontmatter, so config fails open (B6). Share one value parser that rejects mismatched quotes, and add config rows for `"node'` and `'node`.

Comment stripping only recognises a space before `#` (`split(" #")`), in both `strip()` and the frontmatter line at line 102. YAML also allows a tab before `#`, and a value with a tab-led comment is then rejected as malformed or unknown. Strip comments on `\s#` in the shared parser and add tab-comment rows for flow, block and frontmatter.
